title: rest export: CSV has no UTF-8 BOM, so Excel opens a Chinese (or any non-ASCII) export as garbled text
body:
repo:hotcrm#1 · huangyiirene · session_01J8VVAjSbVCwcyoaiYadYJW

Filing gate **① a reproduced defect** (user-visible), measured from HotCRM 6.4.0 (main b820306) on platform **18.5.0** during the end-to-end customer test.

## What happens

A user exports a list to CSV and double-clicks the file. Excel on Windows (and Excel for Mac) reads a CSV with no byte-order mark in the system ANSI code page, so the Chinese column headers and values come out garbled. The export itself is correct UTF-8.

| Request | Answer |
|---|---|
| `GET /api/v1/data/crm_account/export?format=csv` with `Accept-Language: zh-CN` | 200, `text/csv; charset=utf-8`, first bytes `E5 88 9B E5 BB BA …` (`创建时间,创建人,…`), no `EF BB BF` |
| Same with `format=xlsx` | 200, a workbook that opens correctly |

Row counts match the list for every role tried (admin, rep, agent, marketing; accounts, contacts, leads, opportunities, cases), so this is only the encoding signal.

## Seam

`packages/rest/src/data-action-routes.ts:1573` (origin/main 86350e12) sets `Content-Type: text/csv; charset=utf-8` and streams the rows without a leading BOM. Excel ignores the HTTP charset once the file is on disk.

## Suggestion

Write `﻿` before the header row for `format=csv` (or offer a documented `bom=true` and make it the default for the console's export button). JSON and XLSX are unaffected.

## Business reason

The first thing a finance or sales operations user in a Chinese, Japanese or European org does with an export is open it in Excel. Today every non-ASCII header and value is unreadable, and the workaround (Data → From Text → UTF-8) is not something a business user knows.

**Reader:** the objectstack server lane (rest export).

**Grade suggestion: `priority:p2`**: every CSV export in a non-English org. **Size: S.**

**Dedupe:** `gh api search/issues` on `repo:objectstack-ai/objectstack is:issue` with `csv export BOM`, `export csv excel garbled`, `csv utf-8 bom`: hits #29010, #25873, #17962, #19978 (driver-sqlite BOM strip on read), #3358. None covers the export's missing BOM.
